# GROK — the standalone export, measured

*Generated by `analysis/grok_export.py`. Do not hand-edit.*
Schema and the four-archive asymmetry table: `analysis/GROK_EXPORT.md`.

**145 conversations, 1,201 turns**, 2025-08-13 .. 2026-08-16, plus **2,007 media generations** (1,346 video, 661 image) over 66 days.

## 1. It is not the same record as the Grok chats in the Twitter export

Endorphin's reading when he supplied the file, and the reason this section is
first. The test is written to fail: if the standalone export were the X-side
conversations under another schema, turns would coincide — same moment, same
length. A five-minute tolerance is far looser than a real duplicate would need.

| | standalone | Grok on X |
|---|---:|---:|
| turns | 1,201 | 2,818 |
| conversations | 145 | 431 |
| first .. last | 2025-08-13 .. 2026-08-16 | 2024-12-07 .. 2026-07-29 |
| distinct days | 97 | 162 |
| turns inside the overlap window | 1,197 | 418 |

The two records overlap in time from **2025-08-13T02:39:50** to **2026-07-29T21:33:51**, and share **12 calendar days**. Inside that window:

- **Exact-length coincidences within five minutes: 0.**
- The closest any standalone turn comes to any X-side turn is **1.3 minutes**; the median separation is **7.5 days**.

**Two records, no shared turns.** They are different practices on different
surfaces, and the standalone one starts about eight months later. Do not
add the turn counts together and do not treat either as a sample of the
other.

**But they are not separate sessions in time, and that is the more interesting half.** The closest pair — an exchange on X stamped 2025-09-09T14:05:30, then a 34-character human turn in the standalone app 1.3 minutes later — is one person moving between two surfaces inside the same minute, not two independent habits. The records are disjoint; the activity is not necessarily. Anything that treats a gap in one archive as a gap in his attention has to check the other first.

## 2. The cue length holds — and the opener control breaks, the other way

`FINDINGS.md`'s frame rests on a median human turn of **55 characters** across 134,063 NovelAI blocks. `TWITTER.md` §1 re-measured it off-platform at **58**, and found the *opener* — a turn with nothing before it, which cannot be a response to a generation — at **55**, indistinguishable. That is the result that cost the median its status as evidence for turn-taking.

| | n | median | mean | <50 | 50–200 | 200–600 | 600+ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| standalone, after an assistant turn | 442 | **61** | 532 | 44.3% | 32.6% | 11.1% | 12.0% |
| standalone, conversation opener (control) | 145 | **121** | 1576 | 28.3% | 40.0% | 10.3% | 21.4% |

The cue survives a fourth platform: **61 characters** against 55 on NovelAI and 58 on X. But the opener here is **2.0× longer than the follower**, where on X the two were the same number. So the X-side null was a property of *that* practice — 431 one-minute lookups, where the opener is the whole errand — and not a general fact about openings. **The standing note that position in the exchange does not move the number needs the qualifier `on X`.** It does move it here, in the direction the turn-taking frame predicts, on the archive where conversations are long enough for position to mean anything.

The mean-median gap is the pasted-block signature again: mean 532 against median 61. Screen on length before reading anything into human character counts, exactly as `analysis/pasted.py` does on the NovelAI side.

## 3. Latency, recoverable for the first time in this project

`FINDINGS.md` §11: NovelAI stores no per-block timestamps, so tempo is gone. `TW_EXPORT.md`: the X-side agent turn copies the request stamp exactly, 1,409/1,409, so model latency is zero everywhere by construction. Here:

- Human→assistant stamp pairs: **587**, of which **0** share a stamp. The assistant turn is stamped independently.
- Turnaround: median **22.2s**, p10 3.1s, p90 58.8s.
- The server's own thinking window, on the **494** responses that carry one: median **14.7s**, p10 3.5s, p90 49.2s, max 482s.

The two agree in shape, which is the check: an explicit generation window of 15s median sitting inside a 22s median turnaround is what a real stamp looks like. **This is the one measurement the project has wanted since §11 and has never had.** It is still not the NovelAI practice being measured — see §5 — so it bounds nothing about the fiction sessions.

## 4. There is a tree, and `TW_EXPORT.md`'s asymmetry does not generalise

Every response but a conversation root carries `parent_response_id` (1,058 of 1,201; 2 point at a parent that is not in the export). That is a branch structure, which the X-side does not have and which is the entire basis of `FINDINGS.md`'s method.

- **32 sibling sets** across **21 conversations** — a parent with more than one child, i.e. the same point in the conversation taken twice.
- Kinds: **21** re-roll, **11** prompt edit. Assistant siblings are re-rolls; human siblings are edited prompts.
- **8 sibling sets span more than one model** — the same prompt answered by two Grok versions, side by side, in the record. `CLAUDE.md` says this corpus cannot benchmark models because settings moved with model choice; here the prompt is held fixed by construction.

**The limit, and it is a hard one.** `leaf_response_id` — which would say outright which branch was kept — is null on 143 of 145 conversations. The fallback is to ask which sibling was continued, and it is partial: **6** where 0 continued, **15** where 1 continued, **10** where 2 continued, **1** where 3 continued (of the siblings in the set). So selection is readable in the sets where exactly one branch grew, unreadable where none did, and where two or more grew there was no rejection to read — both branches were kept and continued. **Do not run `FINDINGS.md`'s reachability method here unmodified**; walk children forward, do not walk `prevBlock` back.

And the sample is small. 32 sibling sets against the NovelAI corpus's whole undo tree is not a rejection dataset; it is proof that the field exists and a handful of instances. **The right use of it is to check whether a NovelAI finding reproduces, not to found anything new on it.**

## 5. It is a fourth practice, not more of any of the others

145 conversations, median **4 turns** and **1.6 minutes**, with a p90 of 5.9 hours and a longest of 194 turns. The assistant writes **2,211,569 characters** against the author's **463,515**, a 4.8:1 split.

- **Models named on the response**, which no other archive here does: `grok-4` 434, `grok-420-computer-use-sa` 256, `grok-3` 170, `grok-4-auto` 71, `grok-420` 60, `grok-4-1-thinking-1129` 42.
- **Effort setting** recorded on 508 responses: high 399, low 100, auto 9. This is the closest thing to a sampler setting in any non-NovelAI archive, and it is a three-value switch, not a dial — nothing resembling `analysis/sweeps.py` can be run on it.
- **220 responses carry web search results** and **114 carry file attachments** — the model is reading documents and the live web, which nothing in the NovelAI corpus does.
- **2,007 media generations** (2025-08-12 .. 2026-05-04) sit in the same export and are a separate substrate again — image and video prompting, not turn-taking with text.

Against the X-side's 431 chats at a median of 4 turns and one minute, and against NovelAI documents of 3,341 blocks: this sits between them. Long argumentative exchanges and an evaluation apparatus run across months, next to utility lookups and image work, in one record. **`CLAUDE.md`'s rule holds a fourth time — do not read it as more of the corpus.** *(That characterisation is from conversation titles, turn counts and durations. No reading pass has been done on this archive, and none should be assumed by anything that cites this file.)*
